subject: Nanotechnology
title: Gallium Nitride Power Electronics
description: A fast breakdown of Gallium Nitride Power Electronics for builders.

hook.text: Your laptop charger used to be the size of a brick — gallium nitride shrunk it to a deck of cards.

buildup.text: GaN has a wide band gap — it handles higher voltages and frequencies than silicon while losing less energy as heat.

discovery.text: GaN transistors switch in nanoseconds — 10 times faster than silicon, shrinking the inductors and capacitors around them.

twist.text: Growing GaN on silicon substrates creates defects — managing crystal mismatch is the manufacturing challenge.

climax.text: GaN chargers, data center power supplies, and EV inverters are shipping today — replacing silicon quietly.

punchline.text: A wider band gap means smaller, cooler, faster power electronics.

quiz.question: Why are GaN chargers smaller than silicon ones?
options: GaN is a lighter element than silicon
Faster switching in GaN shrinks the passive components needed
GaN chargers skip voltage conversion entirely
